title: Blind Eagle-Linked Loader Uses GitHub, VBScript, PowerShell and InstallUtil to Deploy AsyncRAT
content_md: Researchers have uncovered a Blind Eagle-linked malware operation that uses GitHub repositories , phishing lures, VBScript, PowerShell, and the legitimate Windows InstallUtil utility to deploy AsyncRAT on victim systems. The investigation began with the GitHub account cabeto850128, which was used to host components of a malware loader. The account’s comicsam repository stored an AutoIt interpreter and separate script content, allowing attackers to update malicious logic without repeatedly uploading a modified executable. A GitHub commit exposed an email address in its author metadata. Researchers used that address as a pivot and found it in a leaked infostealer log collection. Additional compromise intelligence linked the address to a device named “Ghost,” which had apparently been infected by an unrelated information-stealing malware family. The recovered stealer log provided a rare look into what appears to be an attacker-side workstation. It contained browser artifacts, local directories, phishing templates, RAT-building tools, bulk-email software, hosting records, and evidence of commercial crypter use. The findings suggest that the GitHub repository was only one part of a wider malware delivery pipeline. Blind Eagle Deploys AsyncRAT The analyzed samples were self-extracting RAR archives disguised as legitimate-looking files, including invoice and PDF-themed attachments. When opened, the archive launches a VBScript-based dropper. The initial script uses wscript.exe to exe
